narrativeReportMd:
# BiologicallyDerivedProduct R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps the same `BiologicallyDerivedProduct` resource identity but substantially reshapes its local content model. R4 instances that use `productCategory`, `status`, `quantity`, `collection.source`, `processing`, `manipulation`, or `storage` need transformation before R6 validation.

## Scope
The assessment covers the local resource StructureDefinitions and related local terminology files. Base-resource and datatype changes are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The main migration work is representation conversion from primitive or legacy backbone fields into R6 `CodeableConcept`, `Coding`, split source references, `Range`, and generic property or traceability structures. Several R6-only traceability fields cannot be losslessly represented in R4 without extensions.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact local changes are the `productCategory` representation change, `status` to `productStatus` rename/type change, removal of processing/manipulation/storage backbones, and introduction of R6-only traceability/property content.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed where R4 detailed operational data has no direct R6 field, and where terminology or business rules must decide mappings for status, category, storage, processing, manipulation, and product code.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many changes could have been less disruptive by retaining deprecated legacy elements while adding the R6 structures. The R6 design appears to target richer MPHO traceability and product labeling semantics, but it is not wire-compatible with R4.

## Follow-up analysis
Follow-up should cover inherited base changes, search parameters, and any official cross-version maps or implementation-guide rules for MPHO product migration.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `BiologicallyDerivedProduct` has material local breaking changes despite unchanged resource identity. Top concerns are legacy field removals, `status` and `productCategory` representation changes, and non-lossless R6-to-R4 traceability/property content. The main uncertainty is the absence of official element-level migration maps and ballot rationale.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not a simple validator-version change. Implementers must transform primitive `code` fields to coded datatypes, rename/split fields, decide how to preserve removed processing/manipulation/storage/quantity details, and handle R6-only traceability fields through extensions or loss-aware downgrade rules.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, type, binding-strength, and local terminology differences because both StructureDefinitions and related local CodeSystems/ValueSets were inspected. Confidence is medium for intent and best mappings because official narrative diffs, ballot notes, terminology-server expansions, and element-level R4-to-R6 ConceptMaps were not available.

findings.title: `productCategory` changed from a single required-bound primitive code to repeating CodeableConcepts

oldState.summary: Optional single primitive `code` with required binding to `ValueSet/product-category|4.0.1`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 CodeSystem includes `organ`, `tissue`, `fluid`, `cells`, and camel-case `biologicalAgent`.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represents the category as a single primitive JSON string such as `"organ"`, constrained by a required value set.

newState.summary: Optional repeating `CodeableConcept` with example binding to `ValueSet/product-category`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 CodeSystem uses hyphenated `biological-agent` and adds `mpho`; the binding is only example, so base validation no longer requires these codes.

semanticText.short: A category or classification of the product
semanticText.definition: A category or classification of the product. Products may be assigned multiple categories, for example a human heart valve can be categorized as an 'MPHO' and 'tissue'.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 represents categories as an array of `CodeableConcept` objects and explicitly supports multiple classifications.

facts.note: The comparable category concept appears to have changed code spelling; R6 also adds `mpho`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element path is unchanged, but its datatype, JSON shape, cardinality, binding strength, and local category code system content changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a hard wire-format break for any R4 instance carrying `productCategory`: the R4 primitive string is not the R6 repeating `CodeableConcept` array shape. It is also a downgrade risk because R6 can contain multiple categories, free-form CodeableConcept codings, and `mpho`, none of which fit the single required-bound R4 primitive code without choosing or losing information.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Product category can influence inventory, handling, and clinical interpretation; incorrect or lossy mappings may misclassify the product.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow multiple product classifications and richer coding for medical products of human origin.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 primitive category as deprecated and add a new repeating CodeableConcept category element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: the R4 `0..1 code` category cannot express multiple classifications or richer coded category metadata. A less-breaking design was possible, but it would have left category facts split across legacy and modern fields. Because that duplication creates real validation and receiver-precedence ambiguity, the breaking replacement is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `productCategory` as the legacy `code` field, including a defined mapping for `biologicalAgent`, and add a new repeatable `CodeableConcept` field for richer and multiple categories. This would preserve most R4 instances. The downside is that category could be asserted in two places; profiles and implementations would need precedence and consistency rules, and the deprecated primitive representation might never fully disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve R4 instances but create duplicate category representations and reconciliation rules that could persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `productCategory` as `0..1 code` with a required binding.
R6 defines `productCategory` as `0..* CodeableConcept` with an example binding.
evidence.quote: Products may be assigned multiple categories

evidence.detail: The R4 category code `biologicalAgent` is not present under that spelling in the inspected R6 CodeSystem; R6 has `biological-agent` and `mpho`.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments are intentionally minimal. The first shows the R4 primitive form; the migration example shows the expected R6 array-of-CodeableConcept shape and the likely spelling update for `biologicalAgent`.

findings.narrativeMd: `productCategory` kept its path but changed representation. Existing R4 JSON, generated classes, FHIRPath assumptions, database columns, and enum switches that treat the field as one primitive code will not work against R6 data. The change also alters conformance because the category value set is no longer required in the base resource.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance with `"productCategory":"organ"` or `"biologicalAgent"` is not R6-valid because R6 expects a repeating `CodeableConcept`. R6 instances with multiple categories, local codings, or `mpho` cannot be reduced to the R4 field without selecting one code or using an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform the primitive code into a one-element `CodeableConcept` array. Establish a terminology rule for `biologicalAgent` to `biological-agent`, and decide whether to add `mpho` when source data implies MPHO. Downgrade transforms must choose a preferred category or preserve extras in extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer model solves a real expressiveness gap, especially multiple categories, but a transitional retained primitive element or official ConceptMap would have reduced migration risk.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm whether `biologicalAgent` to `biological-agent` is an intended direct replacement before applying automatic terminology conversion.

findings.title: `status` was replaced by `productStatus` with Coding and a different status code system

oldState.summary: Optional primitive `code` named `status`, required-bound to R4 product-status with `available` and `unavailable`.

semanticText.definition: Whether the product is currently available.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 status is a simple primitive code at `BiologicallyDerivedProduct.status`.

newState.summary: Optional `Coding` named `productStatus`, example-bound to biologicallyderived-product-status with `available`, `unavailable`, `processed`, `applied`, and `discarded`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 uses `http://hl7.org/fhir/biologicallyderived-product-status`, not the R4 `http://hl7.org/fhir/product-status` system.

semanticText.definition: The current status of the product.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 status moved to `productStatus` and carries a full `Coding`, allowing a system URI and additional status values.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The names and definitions both describe current product availability/status, and R6 expands the same concept into `productStatus`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 JSON that uses `status` is invalid under R6 because the element is absent and the replacement is a different name and datatype. Generated enum properties and switch logic also break. R6 statuses such as `processed`, `applied`, and `discarded` do not fit the R4 required value set.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Status can drive whether a product may be used, discarded, or traced; wrong mapping can affect workflow and inventory safety.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that the status is product-specific and allow a richer coded status lifecycle.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4 `status` as a deprecated availability code while adding R6 `productStatus` Coding.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of a system-qualified product lifecycle status with values beyond `available` and `unavailable` is reasonable. The old field could not carry the new code system or lifecycle states. Retaining it would be a real compatibility bridge, but status conflicts can affect use, discard, and inventory workflow decisions, so the less-breaking alternative has material safety and interoperability tradeoffs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept optional `status` with the R4 two-code value set and added `productStatus` for richer lifecycle state. That would preserve R4 instances and permit dual population during transition. The tradeoff is that receivers would need explicit rules for conflicts such as `status = available` with `productStatus = discarded`, and old implementations might continue to ignore the more precise lifecycle field.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would avoid wire breakage for old instances but risk conflicting lifecycle and availability statuses.

evidence.detail: R4 has `status` as `0..1 code` with required binding to `ValueSet/product-status|4.0.1`.
R6 has `productStatus` as `0..1 Coding` with example binding to `ValueSet/biologicallyderived-product-status`.
R6 adds `processed`, `applied`, and `discarded` to the biologically derived product status lifecycle.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment uses the `Coding` JSON shape. Downgrade of `discarded`, `processed`, or `applied` to R4 would require a local policy because R4 only has `available` and `unavailable`.

findings.narrativeMd: `status` is not merely rebound; it is removed and replaced by `productStatus`. Implementers with generated R4 models must rename the property, convert primitive code to `Coding`, and account for the new status code system and lifecycle values.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing `status` is old-valid/new-invalid. An R6 instance containing `productStatus` with new lifecycle values is R6-valid but cannot be expressed in R4's required-bound primitive without loss or extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `available` and `unavailable` to R6 `Coding` values using `http://hl7.org/fhir/biologicallyderived-product-status`. Define explicit downgrade rules for `processed`, `applied`, and `discarded`; do not silently map all three to `unavailable` without business review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer lifecycle model is useful, but an official dual-field deprecation period or ConceptMap from R4 `product-status` to R6 `biologicallyderived-product-status` would have made migration safer.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 package includes a ConceptMap from biologically derived product status to generic resource status, not an R4-to-R6 element/value migration map.

findings.title: `collection.source` was split into `sourcePatient` and `sourceOrganization`

oldState.summary: One optional `Reference` element named `source`, targetting Patient or Organization.

semanticText.definition: The patient or entity, such as a hospital or vendor in the case of a processed/manipulated/manufactured product, providing the product.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 uses one polymorphic reference slot for either the biological source patient or an organization/entity.

newState.summary: Two separate optional reference elements: `sourcePatient` targetting Patient and `sourceOrganization` targetting Organization.

semanticText.short: The patient who underwent the medical procedure to collect the product / The organization that facilitated the collection

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates source identity from facilitating organization and includes a privacy comment on identifiable patient sources.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old single element's two reference targets correspond directly to the two R6 split elements.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance with `collection.source` is invalid in R6 because that path no longer exists. Mapping is usually deterministic based on the reference type, but R6 can contain both patient and organization, while R4 had only one slot.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Source identity has traceability and privacy implications, especially for identifiable donors or patients.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate biological source patient from facilitating organization and make privacy-sensitive semantics explicit.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating the biological source patient from the facilitating organization is a reasonable R6 goal and supports clearer privacy and traceability semantics. A retained `collection.source` would preserve old instances, but it would also preserve the R4 ambiguity and allow contradictory source data across old and new fields. That makes the less-breaking design only partial.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would keep `collection.source` as a deprecated Patient-or-Organization reference and add the two precise R6 references. Patient-valued legacy sources could map to `sourcePatient`, and Organization-valued legacy sources to `sourceOrganization`. The tradeoff is duplicate same-resource representations: receivers would need rules for whether the old field, the split fields, or both are authoritative, and R6 instances with both source patient and organization still would not fit cleanly into the single R4 field.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 input but creates overlapping source fields and conflict rules, especially when R6 carries both patient and organization.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `collection.source` as a Patient or Organization reference.
R6 defines a Patient-only source element and comments on access controls for identifiable patient sources.
R6 defines a separate Organization-only source element.

examples.examplesMd: A Patient reference maps to `sourcePatient`; an Organization reference maps to `sourceOrganization`. R6 instances with both cannot be represented in R4 without extensions or a policy choice.

findings.narrativeMd: The source element moved from one target-polymorphic reference to two semantically distinct fields. This will break path-based access, generated models, queries, and transforms that expect `collection.source`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 content with `collection.source` is old-valid/new-invalid. R6 content can be downgraded only if at most one of the two split elements is populated or if the extra value is preserved outside the R4 core field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inspect the referenced resource type during migration. Map Patient references to `collection.sourcePatient` and Organization references to `collection.sourceOrganization`. For R6-to-R4, define an extension or precedence rule when both are present.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The split is semantically cleaner, but retaining the old field as deprecated would have allowed lossless ingestion of R4 data during a transition period.

findings.title: `quantity` was removed with no direct R6 replacement

oldState.summary: Optional integer count of discrete units within the product.

semanticText.short: The amount of this biologically derived product
semanticText.definition: Number of discrete units within this product.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has a direct scalar count for discrete units.

newState.summary: No `BiologicallyDerivedProduct.quantity` element is present in R6.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 may be able to express some quantity-like facts through product codes or generic `property`, but there is no direct fixed-path replacement for the R4 count.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 differential and snapshot contain no element named `quantity`; new generic property content is not a direct identity-preserving match.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance that contains `quantity` will fail strict R6 validation because the element is unknown. The runtime risk is moderate because the value is simple but there is no computable destination path.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The number of units may matter for inventory, fulfillment, and administration planning.

justification.inferredGoal: Move product amount semantics into product coding, labeling, packaging, or generic property structures.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional `quantity` as a deprecated discrete-unit count and define how it relates to any R6 property or product-labeling model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of moving amount information into product coding, labeling, or generic properties may be reasonable, but the inspected R6 base definition provides no direct replacement for the R4 integer count. Since the R4 element was optional and simple, retaining it as deprecated would have preserved existing valid instances while R6 introduced more precise modeling elsewhere. The removal therefore looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design would keep `BiologicallyDerivedProduct.quantity` as `0..1 integer`, mark it legacy or deprecated, and add guidance about when a product code, package model, or typed property should supersede it. This would not prevent richer R6 modeling. The main tradeoff is carrying a coarse legacy count that might not align with more precise product-labeling semantics.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Legacy count semantics may be imprecise or duplicate packaging/product-code information, but the compatibility cost is low because the field was optional and had no direct replacement.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `quantity` as `0..1 integer`.
No R6 element with path or id `BiologicallyDerivedProduct.quantity` was present.

examples.examplesMd: The property-based migration example is illustrative only; the inspected R6 property type value set does not include a dedicated discrete-unit-count code.

findings.narrativeMd: `quantity` is a direct removal. Systems that used it for unit counts cannot just rename the field; they need a business mapping or extension.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `quantity` are old-valid/new-invalid in R6. R6 does not introduce a directly equivalent core element, so a lossless R4-to-R6 transform needs an extension or agreed property coding.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory systems should identify all uses of `quantity`, decide whether the value is encoded in `productCode`, a package/labeling artifact, an R6 `property`, or an extension, and test that downstream fulfillment logic still receives the count.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Removal appears avoidable from a wire-compatibility perspective because the element was optional and could have been deprecated without blocking the R6 model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed to choose a sanctioned target because a generic property without a stable code may be hard for receivers to process.

findings.title: R4 processing and manipulation backbones were removed from R6

oldState.summary: R4 has repeatable `processing` details and a single `manipulation` backbone with descriptions, procedures/additives, and time.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can carry collection-time processing that does not change product nature and post-collection manipulation intended to alter the product.

newState.summary: R6 has no `processing` or `manipulation` backbones. Related information may be embedded in `productCode`, `collection.procedure`, or generic `property` entries.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 shifts toward coded product characterization and traceability rather than preserving the R4 event-detail backbones.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: There is no same-path replacement. R6 `productCode`, `collection.procedure`, and `property` may cover some use cases but do not preserve the event backbone identity, repeat structure, additive reference, or free-text/time fields directly.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Strict R6 validators reject R4 instances containing these backbones. The runtime risk is high for systems that display, audit, or make eligibility decisions from processing/manipulation details. R6-to-R4 risk is medium because R6 product codes/properties may imply processing but do not reconstruct R4's detailed structure.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Processing, additives, and manipulation can be clinically significant for product suitability and handling.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent processing/manipulation as part of standardized product characterization and MPHO labeling rather than separate local event backbones.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 processing and manipulation backbones as deprecated while adding R6 product-code and property-based characterization.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of standardized MPHO product characterization is credible, and product codes may intentionally encode processing conditions. However, the R4 backbones carried event detail, additive references, free text, and timing that do not have a direct R6 destination. A retained-deprecated design would avoid immediate data loss for old instances, but it would also risk inconsistent clinical facts between legacy event details and coded characterization. Because the tradeoff is material but the evidence does not explain full removal, the breakage is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would keep `processing` and `manipulation` as optional deprecated backbones while encouraging R6 `productCode` and coded `property` entries for standardized characterization. This would preserve R4-valid data and support gradual migration. The material downside is duplicate product-processing facts in one resource: additives, manipulation timing, and product codes could disagree, receivers would need precedence rules, and deprecated event-detail fields could accumulate indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve detailed legacy events but create overlapping clinically significant representations with product codes and properties.

evidence.detail: R4 defines repeatable processing details with description, procedure, additive, and time.
R4 defines a manipulation backbone with description and time.
R6 contains no `processing` or `manipulation` element paths.
R6 `productCode` definition includes characterization inclusive of processing conditions, additives, volumes, and handling conditions.

property.valueString: Anticoagulant added during collection; CD8 reduction

examples.examplesMd: The migration fragment is not a lossless or normative mapping. It shows the kinds of R6 destinations that may be considered when no direct event-detail backbone exists.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 could record detailed processing and manipulation events directly on the product. R6 removes those structures. This is more than a field rename because R4 had multiple subelements, repeatability for processing, a Substance reference for additive, and timing details.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Any R4 instance with `processing` or `manipulation` is old-valid/new-invalid. Some data may be captured in R6 product codes or properties, but strict round-trip preservation of description, additive reference, and timing is not guaranteed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory existing uses of processing and manipulation. Prefer official product codes when a code fully encodes processing conditions. Preserve residual descriptions, additives, and times in extensions or well-governed `property` codings if receivers can process them. Include tests for multiple processing entries and manipulation timing.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This removal was likely avoidable by retaining optional legacy backbones. If the R6 goal was standard product coding, deprecation plus guidance would have reduced data-loss risk.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Clinical SMEs should review mappings because additives and manipulation can affect product suitability.

findings.title: R4 `storage` backbone was removed and partly replaced by `storageTempRequirements`

oldState.summary: Repeatable storage backbone with description, decimal temperature, required-bound scale code, and duration.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can describe one or more storage instructions, including free text, a single temperature plus scale, and a storage period.

newState.summary: Single optional `Range` named `storageTempRequirements`; no storage description, scale code, duration, or repeat backbone.

semanticText.definition: The temperature requirements for storage of the biologically-derived product.
semanticText.comment: May be extracted from information held in the productCode element.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps only a temperature requirement range and notes that it may be derived from `productCode`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `storageTempRequirements` covers storage temperature requirements but not the full R4 repeatable storage backbone.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `storage` content is rejected by R6. Conversion is not purely mechanical because R4 allowed multiple storage entries, a description, duration, and a temperature scale code; R6 has one `Range` and may rely on `productCode` for other handling conditions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Storage temperature and duration can be critical for product viability and safety.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize temperature requirements as a range and move handling conditions into product codes where possible.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated R4 `storage` while adding `storageTempRequirements` Range.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Modeling temperature requirements as a `Range` is a reasonable improvement over a single decimal plus scale code, and R6 may derive storage handling from product codes. A less-breaking design could preserve R4 storage entries, but storage conditions are safety-sensitive; duplicate temperature, duration, and description fields could disagree with the R6 range or product-code-derived handling. With those material tradeoffs, the breaking replacement is probably justified, though detailed migration guidance remains important.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have added `storageTempRequirements` and left the old repeatable `storage` backbone optional and deprecated. That would preserve R4 instances containing description, temperature, scale, and duration. The tradeoff is validation and safety ambiguity: implementers would need rules for conflicts between old storage temperatures, the new range, product-code-implied handling conditions, and multiple legacy storage entries.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old storage data but create overlapping storage-temperature representations with safety-significant conflict risk.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `storage` as `0..* BackboneElement` with description, temperature, scale, and duration.
R4 storage scale was required-bound to codes `farenheit`, `celsius`, and `kelvin`.
R6 defines `storageTempRequirements` as `0..1 Range` and comments that it may be extracted from `productCode`.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 migration example can only preserve temperature requirements. The R4 description and duration need another target if they are material.

findings.narrativeMd: `storage` changed from a repeatable instruction backbone to a single temperature range. This is a hard validation break and can be a data-loss risk because not all R4 storage subelements have an R6 core destination.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `storage` are old-valid/new-invalid. R6 `storageTempRequirements` can sometimes be downgraded to one R4 storage temperature, but ranges, units, and missing duration/description semantics make round-trip conversion incomplete.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert simple Celsius/Fahrenheit/Kelvin temperatures into `Range` quantities using UCUM units where possible. Preserve storage descriptions, durations, multiple storage conditions, and uncertain scale conversions in extensions or product-code-derived rules. Validate clinically important thresholds after conversion.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The `Range` datatype improves the temperature model, but retaining the old backbone during transition would have avoided rejection of existing storage data and allowed gradual normalization.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R4 code `farenheit` is misspelled in the local CodeSystem; handle this carefully if converting to UCUM Fahrenheit.

findings.title: R6 adds traceability, facility, expiration, procedure, temperature, and generic property content not directly representable in R4

affectedLocation.newPath: BiologicallyDerivedProduct.therapyIdentifier / biologicalSourceEvent / processingFacility / division / expirationDate / collection.procedure / storageTempRequirements / property

oldState.summary: R4 has none of these local elements, aside from partial concepts elsewhere such as `identifier`, `collection`, or `storage`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 lacks core fields for therapy identifier, biological source event, processing facility, division identifier, expiration date, collection Procedure reference, generic typed properties, and R6's storage temperature range.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional elements for MPHO traceability, labeling, collection procedure, temperature requirements, and instance-specific properties.
newState.narrativeMd: The additions are optional for R4-to-R6 validation but become important when downgrading R6 data or maintaining a bidirectional store.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These R6 paths have no same-path R4 equivalents. Some can be approximated by R4 extensions or existing fields, but not by the R4 base resource alone.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The additions do not invalidate R4 data moving forward because they are optional. They are high-impact for downgrade, synchronization, and code generation because R6 instances may contain clinically or regulatory important traceability fields with no R4 core destination.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Traceability identifiers, processing facilities, expiration, and product properties can support donor-to-recipient traceability, recall, and safety workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Support richer MPHO traceability, ISBT 128 labeling, collection procedure linkage, expiration, and flexible product properties.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R6 base alternative is needed because these are optional R6 additions that preserve R4-to-R6 validation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added traceability, facility, expiration, collection-procedure, temperature, and property fields support credible MPHO safety and labeling goals. They do not invalidate R4 instances moving forward because they are optional additions. The compatibility issue is primarily R6-to-R4 representability, so scoring this as a `Partial` backward-compatible alternative would confuse downgrade mitigation with a less-breaking R6 base design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: For this finding, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable: the R6 base design is already forward-compatible for R4 instances. Official R4 extensions, ConceptMaps, or companion records would help older ecosystems preserve the new data on downgrade, but those are cross-version migration strategies, not alternatives that would make the R6 base resource less breaking.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 downgrade needs extensions or companion records, but that is a migration mitigation rather than a backward-compatible base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds a source-event identifier with traceability and donor anonymity comments.
R6 adds repeatable `property` with mandatory `type` and `value[x]` children and multiple choice datatypes.
Several R6 additions carry ISBT 128 mappings, indicating new labeling/traceability semantics.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment uses only optional R6 fields; an R4 base resource has no corresponding core elements.

findings.narrativeMd: R6's new fields are not an R4-to-R6 validation problem, but they are a substantial round-trip and downgrade issue. They carry traceability and labeling semantics that are too important to silently discard.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 instances using these elements are valid R6 but not representable in R4 core JSON without extensions or external records. Parsers generated from R4 will ignore or reject these elements depending on strictness.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For systems that must emit R4, create explicit cross-version extensions or companion records for each R6-only field. Test downgrade/upgrade round-trips for traceability identifiers, expiration, property choice values, and collection procedure references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additions are backward-compatible in the forward direction, but the lack of official R4 extension guidance makes bidirectional compatibility weak.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The business importance of `biologicalSourceEvent` should be reviewed by traceability and privacy stakeholders.

findings.title: `productCode` kept its datatype but changed terminology guidance and semantics toward standardized product characterization

oldState.summary: Optional `CodeableConcept` with example binding but no valueSet in the local differential; definition refers to a kind code and SNOMED CT.

semanticText.short: What this biologically derived product is
semanticText.definition: A code that identifies the kind of this biologically derived product (SNOMED Ctcode).

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 leaves the example binding unspecified in the differential and describes a product-kind code, apparently SNOMED-oriented.

newState.summary: Optional `CodeableConcept` with example binding to `ValueSet/biologicallyderived-productcodes`; definition includes processing conditions, additives, volumes, and handling conditions.

semanticText.short: A code that identifies the kind of this biologically derived product
semanticText.definition: A codified value that systematically supports characterization and classification of medical products of human origin inclusive of processing conditions such as additives, volumes and handling conditions.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 points to a local biologically derived product code system with ISBT-like product description codes and richer product-characterization semantics.

facts.oldValue: identifies the kind of this biologically derived product (SNOMED Ctcode)
facts.newValue: characterization and classification of medical products of human origin inclusive of processing conditions such as additives, volumes and handling conditions

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element path, cardinality, and datatype are unchanged, but the binding target and definition changed materially.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a base validation break because the type and cardinality remain `0..1 CodeableConcept` and the binding remains example. It is still a runtime and conformance risk for systems that assumed SNOMED-style product-kind codes and now encounter MPHO product description codes that may encode processing and handling conditions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Product code interpretation can affect product matching, compatibility checks, storage expectations, and traceability.

justification.inferredGoal: Align product coding with MPHO and ISBT 128-style product description semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base design is required because the path, datatype, cardinality, and example binding strength remain compatible.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning `productCode` with MPHO and ISBT-style product description semantics is consistent with the broader R6 redesign. Because `productCode` remains `0..1 CodeableConcept` with an example binding, R4-era codings can still be represented structurally and the change is not a forward instance-shape break. The main risk is semantic interpretation by applications, making the verdict probably justified with guidance needs rather than avoidable base breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A useful migration approach is to preserve old codings and add R6 product-description codings within the same `CodeableConcept`, with rules for which coding is authoritative. That guidance may be important for interoperability, but it is not a less-breaking R6 base design because the base element already retained its wire shape and permissive binding strength.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Guidance to carry old and new codings together would reduce semantic migration risk but is implementation guidance, not a base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 `productCode` is `CodeableConcept` with example binding and a SNOMED-oriented definition.
R6 `productCode` binds to `ValueSet/biologicallyderived-productcodes` and describes processing, additive, volume, and handling characterization.
The inspected R6 code system contains product-description codes such as red blood cells and HPC apheresis variants.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 coding is structurally a valid CodeableConcept but may not satisfy R4 receivers expecting SNOMED-oriented product-kind semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: `productCode` is structurally stable but semantically different enough to affect business logic. R6 appears to use this field as a richer product description code that can absorb details formerly represented elsewhere.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instances remain structurally valid at this path if transformed as part of the resource. The risk is semantic: validators using only base rules may accept data that application logic misinterprets, and R6 codes may not map cleanly to R4-era expectations.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve existing codings when adding R6 product-description codes. Update terminology services, matching logic, and display rules to recognize `http://hl7.org/fhir/biologicallyderived-productcodes`. Test product-code-driven derivation of storage and processing expectations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because `CodeableConcept` can carry multiple codings, compatibility can be achieved by retaining old codings and adding new ones, but only if implementation guidance states which coding systems are authoritative.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confidence is medium for semantic impact because official narrative guidance was not reviewed.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, derivation, and `DomainResource` base are unchanged. Status changed from draft to active and is reported as notable but not identity-breaking.
No shared pre-existing local element had its minimum cardinality increased. Cardinality-impacting removals and `productCategory` max widening are covered in findings.
`request`, `parent`, and `collection.collector` retained their reference targets. The material `collection.source` target split is covered separately.
No local BiologicallyDerivedProduct-specific invariants were found in the inspected differentials. Inherited `ele-1` and extension constraints are base-artifact concerns.
No local element became a modifier or stopped being a modifier. Modifier behavior on inherited `implicitRules` and `modifierExtension` is out of scope.
`identifier` remains summary. R6 adds `biologicalSourceEvent` as summary, but this is an optional new element rather than a breaking change to an old summary flag.
No local slicing changes were identified on BiologicallyDerivedProduct elements.
No local fixed values, patterns, or defaults were identified in either version for this resource.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were found outside the structural datatype changes already reported.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The StructureDefinition `status` metadata changed from `draft` in R4 to `active` in R6, but the canonical identity, type, base, and abstract flag are unchanged. This does not directly invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance, conformance, and implementation-roadmap processes may treat an active resource differently from a draft resource.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems may want to review identifier system/value conventions because R6 comments recommend globally unique identifiers under an ISO/IEC 15459 Issuing Agency where possible.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited base elements such as `language`, `implicitRules`, `text`, contained resources, and extensions were intentionally excluded from local findings. The inherited `language` binding change should be owned by the base artifact analysis.
